newsitem.title: USA: Space problems postpone trial of Mexican immigrant.
newsitem.headline: Space problems postpone trial of Mexican immigrant.

text.p: The retrial of a Mexican immigrant who spent nearly 14 years on death row awaiting execution for allegedly killing a Houston police officer was postponed on Wednesday because of courthouse space problems.

The trial of Ricardo Aldape Guerra had been set to begin with jury selection on Monday. But court officials said the courtroom of presiding Judge Werner Voigt was too small for the selection process, which will require seating for at least 100 potential jurors.
Voigt told reporters he did not yet know when a courtroom large enough to handle the case would be available, so a new trial date could not be set.
Aldape was convicted of capital murder and sentenced to death by lethal injection in 1982 in the shooting death of a Houston police officer who had stopped a car in which he was riding.

Aldape said the officer was shot by another man, Roberto Carrasco Flores, who later died in a shootout with police. His conviction was thrown out two years ago by U.S. District Judge Kenneth Hoyt, who said police and prosecutors had manipulated evidence and intimidated witnesses to testify against Aldape.

The U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals upheld Hoyt's ruling in August and Aldape was moved off Death Row and in October was granted a new trial by Voigt. He set the original Dec. 2 trial date because he said, "It is not my intention to drag this out any longer than necessary."

Aldape will again be tried for capital murder, for which he faces the death penalty if convicted. His case has become a cause celebre in Mexico where he has been the subject of movies, songs and books, and the Mexican government has intervened in his behalf.
Aldape, now 34, came to the United States illegally from Monterrey, Mexico in 1982 looking for work.
